newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg PM sees more tax coordination in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg PM sees more tax coordination in EMU.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean Claude Juncker said on Tuesday he saw a need for more tax coordination after European monetary union is launched but that this did not mean full harmonisation of tax rules.
"There is no doubt in my mind that the day (when) we will be in monetary union we will have in certain fields the need of bringing closer together our tax provisions..." he told a news conference.
"But this does not mean that we have to harmonise the whole tax landscape we have in the European Union," he said after meeting Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson.

Juncker said a list should be drawn up of what would need to be harmonised. "But we should not give the impression that monetary union does in fact mean that very automatically a member state of monetary union will move into a total federalised political system," Juncker said.
"I don't think we will ever have a United States of Europe, I don't personally want a United States of Europe," he said. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
